headline: Revenue and margins climb, GAAP profit surges
summary_short: Amgen posted Q2 2026 revenue of $10.05B (+9.5% y/y) and GAAP diluted EPS of $4.37 (+65% y/y), with GAAP operating margin expanding 6.5 points to 36.8%; non-GAAP diluted EPS was $6.29 (+4% y/y).
summary_long: Revenue rose 9.5% y/y to $10.05B on broad volume growth (22 products up double digits). GAAP operating margin expanded 6.5 points to 36.8%, driven by a 7% y/y drop in cost of sales from lower acquisition-related amortization; non-GAAP operating margin slipped 0.5 points to 48.4% on higher R&D/SG&A tied to MariTide and Horizon integration. GAAP net income rose 66% to $2.38B (diluted EPS $4.37, +65% y/y); non-GAAP diluted EPS was $6.29 (+4%). Free cash flow nearly doubled to $3.5B; cash rose to $14.0B. FY2026 guidance: revenue $38.2-$39.4B, GAAP EPS $15.80-$17.08, non-GAAP EPS $22.30-$23.50.

drivers.explanation: CEO cited strong performance across the business, with six key growth drivers up 26% y/y contributing nearly 70% of product sales, and expressed confidence in growth as pipeline programs advance toward Phase 3.
Product sales grew 9% on volume growth; 22 products delivered at least double-digit growth and 17 products are annualizing above $1 billion in quarterly sales.
GAAP cost of sales fell 7% y/y and 4.8 points as a percentage of product sales, driven by lower acquisition-related amortization, partly offset by higher profit-share and manufacturing costs.
GAAP operating margin expanded 6.5 points to 36.8%, primarily reflecting the lower cost-of-sales ratio from reduced acquisition-related amortization.
The release attributes GAAP EPS growth to higher revenues; a 5.5-point higher tax rate (14.2% vs 8.7%) partially offset the gain from higher pretax income.

Free cash flow nearly doubled to $3.5B from $1.9B, reflecting the one-time final repatriation tax payment made in Q2 2025 plus current-period business performance, partly offset by working-capital timing.
Not explained in the release; the filing does not attribute the modest y/y increase in long-term debt to any specific financing action.
Not explained in the release; the filing does not attribute the sharp y/y increase in the current portion of debt to any specific driver.
